fields.label: Is the client using less than 1 teaspoon (5g) of salt per day?

fields.text:
"Reducing Salt Intake"
▪b Target: less than 1 teaspoon (5g) per day
▪ Eating too much salt can raise your blood pressure, increase your risk of heart disease, and make it harder to control your blood sugar.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Limit salt intake to protect your heart and blood sugar control

Why: Too much salt raises blood pressure, increases risk of heart disease, and can worsen diabetes control

When: Every day, with every meal and snack

Where: At home and when eating out, be mindful of hidden salt in processed and restaurant foods

How: Keep salt below 5 grams (1 teaspoon) per day, avoid adding extra salt, choose fresh foods, read labels, and use herbs and spices for flavor instead

fields.label: Is the client using less than 5 teaspoons of sugar per day?

fields.text:
"Reducing Sugar Intake"
▪ Target: less than 5 teaspoons per day
▪ Too much sugar raises blood sugar levels, increases the risk of diabetes complications, and harms heart health.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Limit sugar intake to control blood sugar and protect your health

Why: Too much sugar raises blood sugar levels, increases the risk of diabetes complications, and harms heart health

When: Every day, with all meals and drinks

Where: At home and when eating out. Watch for hidden sugars in drinks, snacks, and processed foods.

How: Keep added sugar as low as possible, avoid sugary drinks and sweets, choose water or unsweetened drinks, eat whole foods, and read food labels of processed foods and drinks.

fields.label: Does the client exercise for at least 30 minutes per day until sweating?

fields.text:
"Increasing Physical Activity"
▪ Target: at least 30 minutes per day, until sweating
▪ Exercise helps lower blood pressure, control blood sugar, strengthen the heart, and maintain a healthy weight.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Engage in regular physical exercise to improve your health

Why: Exercise helps lower blood pressure, control blood sugar, strengthen the heart, and maintain a healthy weight

When: At least 30 minutes most days of the week

Where: At home, outdoors, or any safe place convenient for you

How: Start with simple activities like walking, cycling, or stretching, increase gradually, and stay consistent
